test_title: PYST 4: Selection Post (Matric Level) - Quant (Held On 28 Jul, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: maths
question: A student scored 72 marks in an exam and failed by 8 marks. If the pass percentage is 40%, what was the total mark?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Pass Marks = Marks Scored + Failing Marks = 72 + 8 = 80

Given, 40% of Total Marks = 80

1% of Total Marks = 80 ÷ 40 = 2

100% (Total Marks) = 2 × 100 = 200

**∴ The correct answer is 200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marks Scored = 72

Failing Marks = 8

Passing Percentage = 40%

**Formula Used:**

Total Marks = (Passing Marks ÷ Passing Percentage) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/06f97f3749695cac84ee19fbc9a1104058d34d7cac04854249e905198130ffd2.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Passing Marks = Marks Scored + Failing Marks

⇒ Passing Marks = 72 + 8 = 80

⇒ Let the total marks be x.

⇒ 40% of x = 80

⇒ (40 ÷ 100) × x = 80

⇒ x = (80 × 100) ÷ 40

⇒ x = 2 × 100

⇒ x = 200

**∴ The correct answer is 200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

To simplify calculations, remember common fractions: 40% = 2/5, 20% = 1/5, 25% = 1/4, and 50% = 1/2.

Percentage Change Formula

Percentage Change = [(New Value − Old Value) ÷ Old Value] × 100. This is useful for profit, loss, and growth questions.

Base Change Rule

If A is x% more than B, then B is [x ÷ (100 + x)] × 100% less than A.</p
